title: Design an Enterprise Network Intrusion Detection System (100 Gbps+)

spark.summary: Design an Enterprise Network Intrusion Detection System monitoring 100 Gbps+ across global data centers, detecting lateral movement and C2 beaconing in real time with automated SOAR containment.
spark.keyTakeaway: If credentials or tokens are verified at the edge, deploy DPDK/Suricata Edge Sensors at core optical TAPs, stream compact L7/flow telemetry over Kafka to Flink behavioral detectors, and archive to ClickHouse SIEM with CMDB-guarded SOAR.
spark.byteSummary:
Monitoring 100+ Gbps of enterprise east-west and north-south traffic cannot rely on shipping raw PCAPs to a central cloud—that would double backbone bandwidth.

Instead, Core Switches mirror traffic via optical TAPs to local DPDK/Suricata Edge Sensors that extract compact L7 metadata (DNS, HTTP, JA4) and NetFlow summaries (~50:1 reduction). A Kafka Telemetry Bus feeds Flink Lateral Movement & C2 Beaconing Detectors enriched by a Threat Intel Bloom Filter and ML Anomaly Scorer.

Confirmed alerts persist to a ClickHouse SIEM Lake and trigger SOAR Auto-Containment via Firewall/NAC blocks.

learningJourney.title: 100 Gbps+ Telemetry Reduction Math
learningJourney.purpose: Avoid saturating WAN links by extracting metadata at edge sensors.

explanation.foundation: 100 Gbps = 12.5 GB/s of raw packets (~15M packets/sec).
explanation.core: Shipping raw PCAPs centrally is infeasible.
explanation.deepDive: DPDK/Suricata Edge Sensors parse packets locally and emit only structured JSON/Protobuf events (Zeek L7 + NetFlow + alerts), achieving a 50:1 reduction to ~250 MB/s on Kafka.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design an Enterprise Network Intrusion Detection System (100 Gbps+) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If credentials or tokens are verified at the edge, deploy DPDK/Suricata Edge Sensors at core optical TAPs, stream compact L7/flow telemetry over Kafka to Flink behavioral detectors, and archive to ClickHouse SIEM with CMDB-guarded SOAR.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.

options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Threat Intel Bloom Filters in Flink
learningJourney.purpose: Match 5M+ malicious IPs, domains, and JA4 hashes at 500K events/sec.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Threat Intel Bloom Filters in Flink** as the intuition layer for Design an Enterprise Network Intrusion Detection System (100 Gbps+): Match 5M+ malicious IPs, domains, and JA4 hashes at 500K events/sec.
explanation.core: Querying an external Redis or SQL threat-intel database 500K times/sec adds latency. Flink broadcasts a 10 MB Counting Bloom Filter (5M IOCs at 0.1% FP) to every TaskManager's local RAM via a Kafka broadcast state stream, verifying matches against exact RocksDB/ClickHouse before alerting.

Enterprise NIDS blueprint with adaptive eBPF DDoS flood sampling, 5-min admin-port lateral movement detection, and CMDB-guarded SOAR containment.

learningJourney.title: Flink Lateral Movement & East-West Fan-Out
learningJourney.purpose: Catch compromised hosts scanning internal subnets over SMB, RDP, or SSH.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Flink Lateral Movement & East-West Fan-Out** as the intuition layer for Design an Enterprise Network Intrusion Detection System (100 Gbps+): Catch compromised hosts scanning internal subnets over SMB, RDP, or SSH.
explanation.core: Once an attacker lands on one laptop, they scan internal subnets for SMB (445), RDP (3389), or WinRM (5985). Flink maintains a 15-minute HyperLogLog / Set of distinct internal destination IPs per src_ip; if a workstation's distinct SMB/RDP fan-out exceeds 15 hosts in 5 minutes, it fires a Lateral Movement alert.

learningJourney.title: ClickHouse SIEM Lake & Sub-Second Threat Hunting
learningJourney.purpose: Store petabytes of network telemetry cheaply with <1s forensic search.

explanation.foundation: Think of **ClickHouse SIEM Lake & Sub-Second Threat Hunting** as the intuition layer for Design an Enterprise Network Intrusion Detection System (100 Gbps+): Store petabytes of network telemetry cheaply with <1s forensic search.
explanation.core: Legacy Splunk/Elasticsearch clusters cost millions at 250 MB/s (~21 TB/day). ClickHouse MergeTree tables partitioned by day and ordered by (src_ip, dst_ip, ts) with ZSTD compression shrink 21 TB/day down to ~3 TB/day on NVMe/S3 tiered storage while answering threat-hunting queries in <1s.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, clickhouse siem lake & sub-second threat hunting becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enterprise NIDS blueprint with adaptive eBPF DDoS flood sampling, 5-min admin-port lateral movement detection, and CMDB-guarded SOAR containment.

learningJourney.codeExample:
CREATE TABLE nids_flows (
  ts DateTime64(3),
  src_ip IPv6,
  dst_ip IPv6,
  dst_port UInt16,
  ja4 LowCardinality(String),
  bytes_out UInt64
) ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(ts)
ORDER BY (src_ip, dst_port, ts)
TTL ts + INTERVAL 90 DAY TO VOLUME 's3_cold';

knowledgeChecks.question: Why do 100 Gbps+ NIDS architectures deploy DPDK/Suricata Edge Sensors at data-center core switches instead of streaming raw PCAPs to a central cloud?

options.text: Extracting structured L7/NetFlow metadata at the edge achieves ~50:1 bandwidth reduction (12.5 GB/s -> 250 MB/s), avoiding WAN saturation
options.feedback: Correct! Edge metadata extraction shrinks central Kafka/SIEM bandwidth by 98% while keeping 1h raw PCAPs locally.

options.text: Because Kafka cannot transport binary packet bytes
options.feedback: Kafka transports bytes, but 12.5 GB/s per data center would bankrupt WAN links.

options.text: Because ClickHouse only accepts JSON from edge sensors
options.feedback: ClickHouse accepts Protobuf, Arrow, JSON, and binary formats.
Edge sensors specifically compute JA4 locally.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Edge metadata reduction makes multi-datacenter 100G+ NIDS economically and operationally viable.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does Flink match 5M Threat Intel IOCs against 500K telemetry events/sec without hitting external Redis/SQL latency bottlenecks or Bloom false positives?

options.text: Use a 10 MB local RAM Bloom filter to reject 99.9% of benign traffic, then confirm Bloom hits against a local RocksDB exact set
options.feedback: Correct! Two-stage local Bloom + RocksDB gives nanosecond negative filtering with zero false positives.

options.text: Query ClickHouse synchronously for every single packet
options.feedback: 500K synchronous OLAP queries/sec would crush ClickHouse.

options.text: Broadcast all 5M IOCs inside every NetFlow packet
options.feedback: IOCs are maintained in Flink broadcast state, not packet headers.

options.text: Ignore threat intelligence and rely only on SOAR
options.feedback: SOAR acts on detections; it doesn't replace threat intel matching.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Two-stage in-worker Bloom + RocksDB verification eliminates both network RTTs and Bloom false positives.

knowledgeChecks.question: During a massive UDP DDoS flood, how does an edge sensor prevent CPU saturation from blinding detection of stealthy TLS/DNS/SMB attacks?

options.text: Shut down Suricata completely until the DDoS ends
options.feedback: Shutting down leaves the network completely blind.

options.text: Engage adaptive eBPF sampling on UDP flood ports while preserving 100% inspection of TCP/TLS/DNS handshakes
options.feedback: Correct! Selective flood sampling protects L7 control-plane visibility during volumetric attacks.

options.text: Auto-quarantine all Core Switches via SOAR
options.feedback: Quarantining core switches would take down the entire enterprise.
ClickHouse is downstream and unrelated to sensor CPU load.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Attackers often launch noisy floods as a smokescreen; selective eBPF sampling keeps L7 inspection alive.
